No, it does not use a database transaction. According to [[write-journal]], the guarded write path uses an **in-memory write journal** to achieve all-or-nothing semantics **without requiring a database transaction**. 

The journal itself acts as the transaction log, held in memory for the duration of a single run. When a rollback is needed, the journal can reverse every recorded write in reverse order by restoring previous content or deleting newly created files — all managed through the in-memory structure, not through database transactions.
